bourgescathedral.name: Bourges Cathedral
bourgescathedral.slogan: Thirteenth-century glass that still floods the nave with colour.
bourgescathedral.line: Built between 1195 and about 1230, it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992 for its quintessential Gothic design.

palaisjacquescoeur.name: Palais Jacques-Coeur
palaisjacquescoeur.slogan: A merchant's flamboyant Gothic dream, carved stone by stone.
palaisjacquescoeur.line: Jacques Coeur bought the land in 1443; the palace was finished in 1453, while he sat in prison after his 1451 arrest.

valencaychateau.name: Chateau de Valencay
valencaychateau.slogan: Talleyrand's grand stage, where Napoleon's guests played diplomat.
valencaychateau.line: Napoleon ordered Talleyrand to buy it in 1803, and in WWII it sheltered the Venus de Milo and the Winged Victory of Samothrace.

nohantgeorgesand.name: George Sand's House, Nohant
nohantgeorgesand.slogan: The Berry country house where Chopin wrote and Sand held court.
nohantgeorgesand.line: The whole secret of the study of nature lies in learning how to use one's eyes.
nohantgeorgesand.by: George Sand, who wrote most of her novels at Nohant

noirlacabbey.name: Noirlac Abbey
noirlacabbey.slogan: Cistercian calm in pale stone, almost untouched since the Middle Ages.
noirlacabbey.line: Founded in 1136 by monks from Clairvaux, it is one of the best-preserved Cistercian abbeys in France.
